title: Age-appropriate home adaptation providers
potential_target_entity: Housing-advice centres; specialised conversion and craft businesses (bathroom, access, stair lifts)
consumer_problem: Hard to find trustworthy firms that plan and execute barrier-free conversions well.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Shares the care/ageing moment of need with TOP Pflegeheime (F001) and housing links (F014, F031); execution firms are a new entity type.
competitive_observations: Advice networks advise but do not rate executing firms; lead marketplaces broker jobs without transparent quality criteria.
commercial_hypothesis: Regional specialised firms could value visibility with older clients and relatives.
commercial_unknowns: Number of firms that actually specialise; willingness to pay; partner role of Pflegekassen and advice centres.
population_feasibility: Universe spread across several trades in the Handwerksrolle; specialisation is not registered.
methodology_data_feasibility: Possible inputs: references, certifications, advice-centre referrals, customer surveys; no national quality data.
risks: Incomplete population; inconsistent definitions of 'barrier-free'; safety-relevant works; pay-to-play perception among older buyers.
next_validation_questions: Which register can seed the master list?; Is specialisation observable?; Would advice centres or Pflegekassen cooperate?

title: Ambulatory care services (ambulante Pflegedienste)
target_user: People in need of care living at home and their relatives
consumer_problem: Families must choose a care service quickly, often without comparable quality information.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Close to TOP Pflegeheime (F001) but a different service logic; risk of confusing the two lists.
competitive_observations: Insurer-run care navigators list services and publish official quality results; no consumer-oriented recommendation observed.
commercial_hypothesis: Care services could value regional reputation, also for recruiting scarce staff.
commercial_unknowns: Willingness to pay of mostly small operators; capacity constraints (services may not want more clients).
population_feasibility: Services are licensed by Pflegekassen, so insurer navigators imply a near-complete universe.
methodology_data_feasibility: Official quality indicators, staff ratios, client surveys; comparability across regions to be checked.
risks: Patient safety; quality vs. capacity confusion; regulatory and methodological review.
next_validation_questions: Can insurer navigator data seed a master list?; Which quality data is public and comparable?; Is recommending services useful when capacity is scarce?

title: Energy renovation advisers (Energieberater)
target_user: Private owners planning an energy renovation
potential_target_entity: Energy-advice offices and renovation planners listed as energy-efficiency experts
consumer_problem: Owners struggle to pick an adviser who produces a useful renovation roadmap and secures subsidies.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Connects to EnergieAtlas (F029) and Fertighäuser (F031); distinct from energy-supplier tests.
competitive_observations: The national expert list checks qualification and spot-checks work, but does not compare advisers for consumers.
commercial_hypothesis: Specialised offices could value enquiries and reputation.
commercial_unknowns: Advisers' capacity and willingness to pay; impact of subsidy changes on demand.
population_feasibility: A public national expert list exists; persons vs. firms must be de-duplicated.
methodology_data_feasibility: Qualifications, number of roadmaps, client satisfaction; funding data not public per adviser.
risks: Subsidy rules change often; cross-profession comparability; person-firm duplicates.
next_validation_questions: Can the expert list be used as master list?; Which outcome data is available?; How do subsidy changes affect demand?

title: Solar PV installers for private homes
target_user: Private homeowners considering PV and storage
consumer_problem: Offers are hard to compare; quality of installers and sellers varies.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Energy and housing link (F029, F031); not identical to supplier tests.
competitive_observations: Consumer advice checks individual offers; portals sell leads; no transparent national installer list observed.
commercial_hypothesis: Installers could value trust and qualified enquiries.
commercial_unknowns: Market cycle after the boom; installer consolidation; willingness to pay.
population_feasibility: Installers are not in one register; trade registers and grid-operator lists are partial.
methodology_data_feasibility: Certifications, warranties, customer surveys; installation data in the market master data register is not per installer.
risks: High investment; electrical safety; manufacturer vs. installer role; changing feed-in and subsidy rules; aggressive sales models.
next_validation_questions: How to build the installer universe?; Is demand still growing after rule changes?; How to separate sellers from installers?

title: Digital health applications (DiGA) orientation
consumer_problem: Patients and doctors lack a usable overview of which prescribable app fits which indication.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Apps (F033) and health professions (F008) exist; indication logic is new.
competitive_observations: The official BfArM directory lists assessed apps with evidence status; usability and fit comparison is not its role.
commercial_hypothesis: Manufacturers could value awareness and understandable positioning.
commercial_unknowns: Small, concentrated manufacturer universe; regulatory limits on advertising for medical devices.
population_feasibility: Complete universe in the official directory.
methodology_data_feasibility: Official evidence status, prescription data, user ratings; efficacy must not be re-judged.
risks: Patient safety; data protection; differing indications and evidence levels; medical-device advertising law.
next_validation_questions: Is the universe large enough?; What can FACTS add without re-judging efficacy?; Which advertising rules apply?

title: AI training providers for employees and SMEs
consumer_problem: Hard to judge which AI course builds real, role-relevant competence.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Strong overlap with the existing continuing-education list (F019); sub-segment or update rather than new list.
competitive_observations: Public training search and counselling exists; course-level quality comparison not observed.
commercial_hypothesis: Providers could value reputation for course marketing.
commercial_unknowns: Fast-moving market; provider churn; whether AI-literacy obligations create paying demand.
population_feasibility: Providers are heterogeneous; certified providers (AZAV) are only a subset.
methodology_data_feasibility: Certifications, curricula, participant surveys; content ages fast.
risks: Rapid content ageing; provider vs. course comparison; unsupported compliance promises.
next_validation_questions: Sub-segment of F019 or separate list?; Can outcomes be measured?; Does regulation drive demand?

title: Employer orientation (additional dimension)
consumer_problem: Applicants want trustworthy signals on employer quality.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Direct overlap with existing employer lists (F011, F012); only a precise new dimension could be new.
competitive_observations: Several established rankings, certifications and review seals with visible licence models.
commercial_hypothesis: Employer-branding licence offers exist and are bought.
commercial_unknowns: Saturation; incremental value of yet another seal.
population_feasibility: Company registers exist; segmentation needed.
methodology_data_feasibility: Surveys, reviews, public data on pay transparency.
risks: Cannibalisation; review bias; little new differentiation.
next_validation_questions: Which dimension is truly new?; Does it cannibalise F011/F012?

title: Architects for private building and conversion projects
consumer_problem: Private clients struggle to find an architect who fits project type, budget and region.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Near real-estate (F014) and prefab houses (F031); no architecture product in the portfolio.
competitive_observations: Chamber search lists, awards and platforms offer visibility, not transparent fit.
commercial_hypothesis: Offices could value matching mandates and reference visibility.
commercial_unknowns: Share of offices serving private clients; professional advertising rules.
population_feasibility: Chambers register architects, but online listing is not mandatory.
methodology_data_feasibility: References, awards, client surveys; projects are heterogeneous.
risks: Professional law; incomplete population; heterogeneous projects; weak value of a generic national list.
next_validation_questions: Can chamber data be used?; Which segment (conversion, old buildings) is narrow enough?

title: Workshops and services for used electric cars
target_user: Buyers and owners of used EVs
potential_target_entity: Test services; workshops with EV competence
consumer_problem: Used-EV buyers cannot judge battery health and which workshop can service EVs.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Mobility link (F036); e-bike experience does not transfer to EV methodology.
competitive_observations: Battery certificates exist; workshop competence comparison not observed.
commercial_hypothesis: Workshops could want to show EV competence.
commercial_unknowns: Size of EV-competent workshop segment; growth of the used-EV market.
population_feasibility: Workshop universe exists; EV competence is not registered.
risks: Technical comparability; manufacturer interfaces; small population; investment consequences.
next_validation_questions: How many workshops are EV-qualified?; Is the used-EV market large enough now?

title: Debt-counselling orientation
consumer_problem: People in debt need to find reputable, free help and avoid dubious commercial offers.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Finance and consumer-protection link (F020, F026); vulnerable target group.
competitive_observations: Consumer centres warn against dubious offers and point to recognised services.
commercial_hypothesis: A commercial seal proposition is unclear and could undermine trust.
commercial_unknowns: Recognised centres are mostly publicly/charitably funded and unlikely to buy seals.
population_feasibility: Recognised centres are listed by states/charities.
methodology_data_feasibility: Recognition status, waiting times; quality data sparse.
risks: Financially vulnerable target group; conflicts of interest; legal authorisation; pay-to-play perception.
next_validation_questions: Is there any non-commercial format FACTS could offer?; Would a seal harm trust?

title: Environmental consumer orientation for a defined product group
potential_target_entity: Manufacturers/providers of a defined product group
consumer_problem: Consumers cannot verify green claims.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Existing product-test format (F034, F035); needs a concrete product group.
competitive_observations: Established eco-labels with expert criteria; test organisations with licensing.
commercial_hypothesis: Environmental communication can matter for manufacturers.
commercial_unknowns: Legal room for green claims after EU rule changes.
population_feasibility: Depends on product group.
risks: Greenwashing; non-comparable environmental impacts; tighter rules on sustainability labels.
next_validation_questions: Which product group?; Is a FACTS label legally allowed under the new EU rules?

title: Childcare orientation (Kitas)
consumer_problem: Parents look for quality transparency, but places are scarce.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Education link (F032); university methodology does not transfer.
competitive_observations: Municipal portals offer search and place requests.
commercial_hypothesis: A commercial award may fit public providers only to a limited degree.
commercial_unknowns: Public and church providers dominate; seal demand doubtful.
population_feasibility: Official statistics count facilities; lists are municipal.
methodology_data_feasibility: Staff ratios, concepts; quality inspections not public everywhere.
risks: Child protection; data protection; selection bias; a list does not create places.
next_validation_questions: Is a list useful when parents have no choice?; Who would pay?

title: Heat-pump installers for owner-occupied homes
target_user: Owners replacing a fossil heating system
consumer_problem: Owners must pick an installer for a large, technically demanding investment under changing rules.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Adjacent to EnergieAtlas (F029) and gas suppliers (F030); no installer list in the portfolio.
competitive_observations: Manufacturer installer finders and lead portals exist; national, transparent installer quality list to be checked.
commercial_hypothesis: Installers could value trust signals in a market with consumer uncertainty.
commercial_unknowns: Installer capacity (may not need leads); demand after heating-law and subsidy changes.
population_feasibility: SHK businesses are registered in the Handwerksrolle; heat-pump specialisation is not.
methodology_data_feasibility: Certifications, manufacturer partner status, surveys, complaint data.
risks: Policy volatility; installer shortage makes seals less attractive; manufacturer bias.
next_validation_questions: How many SHK firms install heat pumps?; Is demand stable after policy changes?; Which quality data exists?

title: Property managers for owner associations (WEG-Verwalter)
potential_target_entity: Residential property management companies; certified administrators
consumer_problem: Owner associations must choose and supervise an administrator with large budgets and legal duties.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Adjacent to real estate agencies (F014); different service and decision-maker.
competitive_observations: Associations offer membership signals; reviews are scattered.
commercial_hypothesis: Administrators could value differentiation after the certification requirement.
commercial_unknowns: Market size; fragmentation; willingness to pay.
population_feasibility: Commercial register entries; § 34c licences; association member lists.
risks: Legal disputes between owners and administrators; local markets.
next_validation_questions: How many administrators exist and how many are certified?; Do owners actively compare?

title: Psychotherapy and mental-health access orientation
target_user: People seeking psychotherapy and their families
potential_target_entity: Psychotherapy practices; outpatient clinics; online programmes
consumer_problem: People in distress face long waits and do not know which offer fits.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Adjacent to doctor lists (F002, F003) and health professions (F008).
competitive_observations: Appointment services and therapist search portals exist; quality orientation is sensitive.
commercial_hypothesis: Practices are capacity-constrained; a seal is unlikely to bring value to them.
commercial_unknowns: Seal demand among capacity-constrained practices.
population_feasibility: Licensed psychotherapists are registered with chambers/KVs.
methodology_data_feasibility: Access data (waiting times) more feasible than outcome data.
risks: Vulnerable users; suicide-risk sensitivity; professional law; capacity — a list does not create appointments.
next_validation_questions: Is an access/orientation format more useful than a ranking?; What do professional bodies allow?

title: Day care and 24-hour home care agencies
potential_target_entity: Day-care facilities; agencies placing live-in carers
consumer_problem: Families do not know which agency is legal, fair and reliable.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Extends TOP Pflegeheime (F001) to home settings.
competitive_observations: Agency portals and comparison sites exist; legal grey zones reported.
commercial_hypothesis: Agencies have marketing budgets; seriousness of the segment is the issue.
commercial_unknowns: Share of legally compliant agencies.
population_feasibility: No register for placement agencies.
risks: Labour-law grey zones (posted workers); reputational risk of endorsing non-compliant agencies.
next_validation_questions: Can legal compliance be verified?; Is day care a cleaner sub-segment?

title: Veterinary practices and emergency vet services
consumer_problem: Pet owners face rising costs and fewer emergency services and want trustworthy vets nearby.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Methodology analogue to the doctors list (F002) but a new audience.
competitive_observations: Vet search portals and reviews exist; no transparent national quality list observed.
commercial_hypothesis: Vet practices, increasingly owned by chains, may invest in reputation.
commercial_unknowns: Chain vs. independent practice share; willingness to pay.
population_feasibility: Veterinary chambers register vets; practice-level lists partial.
methodology_data_feasibility: Peer recommendations (doctor-list logic), emergency availability, surveys.
risks: Professional advertising rules; emotional decisions; pay-to-play perception.
next_validation_questions: How many practices exist?; Does the doctor-list methodology transfer?

title: Hearing-aid acousticians and opticians
target_user: Older people and people with hearing or vision impairments
consumer_problem: Large out-of-pocket costs and long-term fitting relationships make the choice of provider important.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Adjacent to health professions (F008).
competitive_observations: Chains dominate visibility; consumer tests occur occasionally.
commercial_hypothesis: Independent businesses could value differentiation from chains.
commercial_unknowns: Chain market share; willingness to pay of independents.
population_feasibility: Craft register (Handwerksrolle) lists master businesses.
risks: Medical-device advertising rules; chain dominance.
next_validation_questions: How many businesses?; Is a consumer survey feasible?

title: Physiotherapy practices
consumer_problem: Patients struggle to find practices with appointments and the right specialisation.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Adjacent to health professions (F008) and rehab clinics (F006).
competitive_observations: Search portals; little quality orientation observed.
commercial_hypothesis: Practices compete for staff more than for patients.
commercial_unknowns: Seal value for capacity-constrained practices.
population_feasibility: Practices approved by health insurers.
risks: Capacity shortage; staff shortage.
next_validation_questions: Is the problem quality or access?

title: Dental practices and implant specialists
consumer_problem: High private co-payments for implants and orthodontics make the choice of dentist consequential.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Close to doctor lists (F002, F003) — check whether dentists are already covered.
competitive_observations: Doctor review portals include dentists; specialist societies certify.
commercial_hypothesis: Dentists with private-pay focus invest in marketing.
commercial_unknowns: Overlap with existing FACTS doctor lists.
population_feasibility: Dental chambers register dentists.
risks: Overlap with existing product; professional advertising rules; YMYL.
next_validation_questions: Does an existing FACTS list already include dentists?

title: Funeral service providers (Bestatter)
target_user: Bereaved relatives; people planning their own funeral
consumer_problem: Relatives must decide quickly, in grief, with little price transparency.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Consumer-advice link (F026); new domain.
competitive_observations: Association quality marks and price portals exist.
commercial_hypothesis: Funeral homes may value trust signals for pre-need contracts.
commercial_unknowns: Acceptability of commercial seals in a grief context.
population_feasibility: Trade associations; business registers.
risks: Vulnerable users (grief); reputational risk; regional fragmentation.
next_validation_questions: Is a pre-need (planning) angle less sensitive?

title: Independent fee-based financial advisers (Honorarberater)
potential_target_entity: Registered fee-based investment advisers and fee-based insurance advisers
consumer_problem: Consumers cannot tell independent advice from commission sales.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Adjacent to retirement provision (F020) and mortgage lenders (F021).
competitive_observations: Register entries prove licence only; fee-advice associations promote the model.
commercial_hypothesis: Fee-based advisers need visibility against commission-based sales.
commercial_unknowns: Small universe; willingness to pay.
population_feasibility: Official intermediary register (IHK/DIHK) lists licence holders.
risks: YMYL; liability; financial-advertising rules.
next_validation_questions: Is the universe large enough?; Does pension reform increase demand?

title: Tax-aid associations and tax advisers for employees/pensioners
target_user: Employees and pensioners filing tax returns
consumer_problem: Private filers do not know whether an association, an adviser or software fits.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Overlaps the tax-adviser product (F016, to_validate) — candidate sub-segment.
competitive_observations: Associations and software comparisons exist.
commercial_hypothesis: Associations compete for members.
commercial_unknowns: Overlap with F016.
population_feasibility: Supervisory authorities register associations.
risks: Cannibalisation of F016; professional law.
next_validation_questions: Sub-segment of F016 or separate?

title: Driving schools
target_user: Young people and parents paying for a driving licence
consumer_problem: Licence costs have risen and pass rates vary; families cannot compare schools.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Mobility link (F036); new entity type.
competitive_observations: Booking and review portals exist; no transparent quality list observed.
commercial_hypothesis: Driving schools compete locally for students.
commercial_unknowns: Effect of a planned licence reform on school economics.
population_feasibility: Driving-school permits are issued by state authorities.
risks: Young target group; reform uncertainty; local markets.
next_validation_questions: Are pass rates available per school?; When does the reform take effect?

title: Independent car workshops (Kfz-Meisterbetriebe)
consumer_problem: Car owners worry about overcharging and quality in repairs.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Mobility link (F036).
competitive_observations: Workshop tests by motoring clubs, booking portals and reviews exist.
commercial_hypothesis: Workshops buy visibility on booking portals.
commercial_unknowns: Saturation by portals; motoring-club authority.
population_feasibility: Trade associations count workshops.
risks: Well-served by tests; local markets.
next_validation_questions: What would FACTS add to existing tests?

title: IT-security service providers for SMEs (NIS2)
target_user: Managing directors of small and mid-sized companies
consumer_problem: Newly regulated SMEs must choose a security provider without expertise to judge quality.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: B2B logic like Innovation/Growth Champions (F013, F018); FOCUS Business audience.
competitive_observations: Certifications (ISO, BSI-qualified providers) exist; comparison for SMEs to be checked.
commercial_hypothesis: Providers are likely to buy trust signals in a compliance-driven market.
commercial_unknowns: Provider universe definition; buyer behaviour.
population_feasibility: No single register; BSI lists of qualified providers are partial.
risks: Liability if a recommended provider fails; fast-changing tech.
next_validation_questions: How many companies fall under NIS2?; Which provider lists exist?

title: All-day schooling and after-school care providers (Ganztag)
potential_target_entity: Providers of all-day care and school programmes
consumer_problem: With a new legal entitlement, parents want to know the quality of all-day offers.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Education link (F032).
competitive_observations: Mostly municipal information.
commercial_hypothesis: Providers are largely public/charitable.
commercial_unknowns: Who would pay?
population_feasibility: Schools are listed by states.
risks: Children; public providers; little choice for parents.
next_validation_questions: Is there real choice for parents?

title: Wallbox and home-charging installers
target_user: EV owners with a private parking space
consumer_problem: EV buyers need a qualified electrician and fair pricing for home charging.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Mobility + energy link (F036, F029).
competitive_observations: Manufacturer installer networks and lead portals.
commercial_hypothesis: Electricians may value leads.
commercial_unknowns: Demand after subsidy end.
population_feasibility: Electrical trade register.
risks: Electrical safety; small ticket size.
next_validation_questions: Does the EV market grow enough to create sustained demand?

title: Pay-transparent employers (EU Pay Transparency Directive)
potential_target_entity: Employers above the directive's size thresholds
consumer_problem: Applicants want to know which employers pay fairly and transparently.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Direct overlap with employer lists (F011, F012) — possible new dimension of an existing product.
competitive_observations: Employer rankings and certifications are numerous.
commercial_hypothesis: Employers may want to signal compliance.
commercial_unknowns: Whether a dimension beats a new list.
population_feasibility: Company registers by size class.
risks: Cannibalisation; crowded market.
next_validation_questions: New list or new criterion for F011/F012?

title: Stair-lift and mobility-aid providers
consumer_problem: High prices and pressure-selling make stair-lift purchases risky.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Sub-segment of home adaptation (M001); adjacent to F001.
competitive_observations: Comparison portals act as lead sellers; consumer centres warn.
commercial_hypothesis: Providers spend heavily on lead generation.
commercial_unknowns: Willingness to accept transparent criteria.
population_feasibility: Few manufacturers, many dealers.
risks: Aggressive sales market; reputational risk; vulnerable buyers.
next_validation_questions: Is a consumer-protection angle compatible with a paid seal?

title: Providers of the new Altersvorsorgedepot (pension investment account)
target_user: Employees and families choosing state-subsidised private retirement products
potential_target_entity: Banks, brokers, insurers and fund platforms offering the new product
consumer_problem: A new subsidised product category replaces Riester; consumers must compare providers, costs and investment options from scratch.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Extends Altersvorsorge (F020); test/list format of FOCUS Money fits; risk of overlap with existing tests.
competitive_observations: Consumer testers and comparison portals will likely cover it quickly; first-mover window is short.
commercial_hypothesis: Providers launching a new product need trust signals and visibility.
commercial_unknowns: How many providers launch; product standardisation reduces differentiation.
population_feasibility: Providers are BaFin-supervised and identifiable.
methodology_data_feasibility: Costs, fund choice, conditions — product data comparable once offers exist.
risks: YMYL; financial-advertising compliance; strong incumbents (consumer tests); product rules may still change.
next_validation_questions: When do offers launch?; How many providers?; What can FACTS add to price comparisons?

title: Repair services for household appliances and electronics (right to repair)
target_user: Consumers with broken appliances or electronics
consumer_problem: Consumers do not know where repair is reliable and fairly priced instead of replacing.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Fits the Deutschland Test service-test format (F034, F035).
competitive_observations: Repair cafés and manufacturer portals; no trusted national quality list observed.
commercial_hypothesis: Independent repairers and manufacturers may want to signal repair quality.
commercial_unknowns: Fragmented small businesses; low marketing budgets.
population_feasibility: Mostly small craft and trade businesses; fragmented.
risks: Fragmented universe; sustainability-claim rules for any 'green' label.
next_validation_questions: Is the provider universe listable?; Does the new EU right-to-repair change consumer behaviour?

title: Independent insurance brokers (Versicherungsmakler)
target_user: Households and small businesses buying insurance
consumer_problem: Consumers cannot judge which broker gives independent, competent advice.
portfolio_fit_and_overlap: Adjacent to insurer tests (F023, F027, F028) — rates intermediaries instead of products.
competitive_observations: Register proves licence only; broker ratings scattered across review platforms.
commercial_hypothesis: A growing broker population competes for clients and may value seals.
commercial_unknowns: Willingness to pay; insurer relationships.
population_feasibility: Official intermediary register (DIHK) lists all brokers.
methodology_data_feasibility: Register data, qualifications, client surveys, complaints.
risks: YMYL; insurer-sponsorship conflicts; liability.
next_validation_questions: Can register data seed the list?; What quality data exists for brokers?
